phonics.note: Optional pronunciation card inside the Speaking station. This is the book's own phonics focus: the ch sound at the beginning and at the end of a word.
phonics.note2: The teaching point is not two different sounds but one sound in two positions: ch at the start (cheese, chair, chips) and ch at the end (lunch, beach, teach, sandwich). Both are the same /tʃ/. Ask the learner to cover their eyes and just listen for where the sound is.

speechScoring.reuse: Same engine as Units 1-8: browser Web Speech API, keyword coverage, bands only, never a numeric grade.
additions: Past forms: accept wasn't / was not, weren't / were not after normalisation.
Numbers matter here: 'two thousand' must not be accepted for 'two hundred'. If the transcript has a different number, show both forms rather than failing silently.
Accept 'there was a' and 'there's a' at Easy; require 'there were' for plurals at Core and above.
The ch contrast is easily misheard: accept 'lunch' with a soft final ch, and never fail an item for the recogniser dropping it.
